Industry-wide practices noted alongside CryptoWild include provably fair certification, security checks, and responsible-gaming tools (self-exclusion, deposit limits), and Bitcoin casino payouts typically advertise 1–24 hour processing though actual times vary by operator. Potential players should weigh large headline bonuses against the fine print on wagering, max cashouts, provider variety, and documented withdrawal or bonus-fulfillment complaints before depositing.

stories.name: Former Speaker Pelosi PayPal sale precedes 27% drop
stories.summary: Nancy Pelosi’s household reported selling 5,000 shares of PayPal on Dec. 30, 2025 in a periodic filing that listed the transaction in the $250,001–$500,000 range (about $295,000 based on that day’s price). In the weeks after the sale, PayPal shares plunged—falling into the low $40s—after weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter results, soft guidance and an unexpected CEO change. By avoiding holding through that drop, the Pelosis averted an estimated roughly 32% decline (about a $96,000 loss) on that position. Ethics experts note there is no public evidence the trade involved nonpublic information and the sale was disclosed under STOCK Act timelines, but the timing has nonetheless renewed bipartisan calls to restrict or ban individual stock trading by lawmakers. The episode reinforces why Pelosi’s household trades remain closely watched and fuels broader public skepticism about elected officials trading individual stocks.
keyPoints: The Periodic Transaction Report documenting the Dec. 30, 2025 sale was filed with the House Clerk and made public on Jan. 23, 2026.
PayPal’s weak fourth-quarter 2025 fundamentals included revenue of $8.68 billion (below the $8.80 billion consensus) and adjusted EPS of $1.23 (missing the roughly $1.28–$1.29 consensus).
The company announced an unexpected leadership change, naming Enrique Lores as PayPal’s new CEO amid the results-driven selloff.

stories.name: Oxfordshire Woman Nearly Dies From Fake Ozempic
stories.summary: Michelle Sword, 47, of Carterton, Oxfordshire, nearly died after injecting a counterfeit Ozempic pen she purchased on Facebook that contained fast-acting insulin instead of semaglutide, causing her blood sugar to fall to 0.2 mmol/L and sending her into a diabetic coma before paramedics stabilized her. She had previously used genuine Ozempic in 2020 to lose two stone but, facing shortages in 2023, paid £150 via PayPal for a month’s supply from an online seller that arrived two days later. Sword later noticed warning signs she missed — the pen kept clicking and she was unsure of the dose — and has published red flags (including packaging errors and lack of eligibility checks) to warn others against buying prescription drugs from unregulated sources. The UK medicines regulator has seized more than 6,500 fake Ozempic products in just over two years, underscoring the wider, potentially deadly problem of counterfeit weight-loss injections.
keyPoints: Sword remained in hospital overnight after the incident until medics could stabilise her blood sugar levels.
She attributed much of the weight regain to menopause and said she had been having a glass of wine with every meal, which contributed to rising weight to around 10½ stone.

Paramedics spent a prolonged period trying to save her life — reports say they worked for over an hour at the scene, with one account noting a 12‑minute wait for emergency services before they arrived.

stories.name: PayPal Names Enrique Lores; Shares Drop 16–20%
stories.summary: PayPal said Enrique Lores, the former HP CEO, will become its CEO on March 1, with CFO Jamie Miller serving as interim CEO until then and David W. Dorman named independent board chair after the board concluded execution under former CEO Alex Chriss was insufficient. The company reported fourth-quarter revenue of about $8.68 billion and non‑GAAP EPS of $1.23 (vs. $1.28 expected); total payment volume rose roughly 6% to $475.1 billion, while active accounts were roughly flat and transaction frequency fell about 5%, and Branded Checkout growth slowed sharply. Management withdrew its prior 2027 targets and guided 2026 to a mid‑single‑digit EPS decline to flat, citing softer U.S. retail demand, high living costs and intensifying competition. The surprise leadership change, the quarterly miss and the downgraded outlook sent the stock down roughly 16–20%, costing about $10 billion in market value and coinciding with unusually heavy bearish options activity. Board and interim management said Lores’ operational focus should help restore discipline and customer‑centric innovation, but investors remain cautious given macro headwinds and big‑tech wallet competition.
keyPoints: Enrique Lores has served on PayPal’s board for nearly five years and had been board chair since July 2024 prior to being named CEO.

Lores is credited for leading HP’s shift beyond traditional PCs into services, subscriptions and AI-enabled "future-of-work" solutions, and for playing a pivotal role in the separation of HP and HPE while strengthening operating discipline and simplifying cost structure.
Interim CEO Jamie Miller explicitly told investors the board’s decision reflected execution issues, saying, “So the board’s decision is based on execution … our execution is just too slow.”

stories.name: Reports: Multiple US Firms Face Securities Investigations
stories.summary: Multiple law firms have launched investor investigations alleging potential violations of federal securities laws across several public companies. The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz announced probes into Plug Power and Picard Medical on behalf of shareholders who lost money. Levi & Korsinsky opened an investigation into PayPal after the company replaced its CEO on February 3, 2026, acknowledged execution problems—particularly in branded checkout—and reported fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results that missed estimates, sending the stock down over 20% intraday. The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith similarly announced investigations for investors in Apollo Global Management and PayPal and is inviting affected shareholders to contact the firm about pursuing claims. All firms are urging investors who suffered losses to reach out to explore potential recovery under the federal securities laws.
keyPoints: Plug Power made a notable company announcement on October 7, 2025 regarding its Chief Executive Officer, which is referenced in the firm’s investigation notice.
Picard Medical’s market-moving disclosure occurred on October 23, 2025 during after-market trading hours, a timing noted in the Frank R. Cruz investigation notice.

Levi & Korsinsky named the replaced PayPal CEO as Alex Chriss and tied the leadership change to the company’s February 3, 2026 announcement that “the pace of change and execution was not in line with the Board's expectations.”

stories.name: PayPal Names Enrique Lores CEO; Shares Plunge
stories.summary: PayPal said its Q4 results missed estimates, reporting revenue of $8.68 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.23, while total payment volume rose to about $475.1 billion and active accounts reached roughly 439 million. Growth in higher‑margin branded checkout slowed to about 1% in the holiday quarter, a concern management and investors highlighted amid competition from Stripe, Apple and others. Citing that the pace of change and execution "was not in line with the Board's expectations," the board named Enrique Lores—former HP CEO and former PayPal board chair—as President and CEO effective March 1, with CFO/COO Jamie Miller serving as interim until then. The results and leadership change prompted a sharp market reaction, with shares plunging roughly mid‑teens to about 18% to lows not seen since early 2017, extending a yearlong decline. PayPal gave modest fiscal‑2026 guidance (reports put EPS around $5.75) and warned of a mid‑single‑digit EPS decline in Q1 and a low‑single‑digit to flat full‑year outcome. The board and new leadership face pressure to accelerate product execution and respond to softer consumer spending and intensifying Big Tech threats to its payments franchise.
keyPoints: This quarter marked PayPal’s first earnings miss in roughly two years, a notable break in the company’s recent streak of meeting or beating estimates.
Management said the underperformance in branded checkout was driven by weakness in U.S. retail, international headwinds and tough year‑ago comparisons in high‑growth verticals.
Total payment volume rose about 9% year‑over‑year (6% on a currency‑neutral basis) to $475.1 billion.

stories.summary: Analysts have grown cautious on PayPal after weak Q4 2025 results and conservative FY2026 guidance: Compass Point moved the stock to Neutral with a $51 target while TD Cowen and Bank of America cut price targets to about $48, citing disappointing exit rates, sluggish branded checkout performance, high investment costs and a surprise CEO change. BTIG has reiterated a Neutral stance in late January/early February, signaling a wait‑and‑see approach rather than a fresh bullish or bearish call. Shares have fallen roughly 19% since Q3 2025, and management expects growth to slow in 2026 while operating expenses rise. PayPal is prioritizing investments in buy‑now‑pay‑later, agentic commerce (including its Cymbio deal) and other engagement initiatives, but several brokers say meaningful returns on those bets are unlikely before fiscal 2027. Overall, analyst coverage skews toward caution with mixed ratings and lower targets until new leadership and execution produce clearer signs of recovery.
keyPoints: Compass Point moved PayPal from a Sell to a Neutral rating while lowering its price target from $55 to $51.
TD Cowen trimmed its price target on PayPal from $65 to $48 as it characterized 2026 as "another transition year" given disappointing exit rates and weak branded checkout performance.

stories.summary: Analysts have been revising views on PayPal this month, with Rothschild & Co Redburn cutting the stock to a sell rating and $50 price target while several other brokers trimmed targets or reaffirmed neutral/hold views. PayPal beat expectations in its last reported quarter (EPS $1.34; revenue $8.42 billion) but the shares have recently traded in the mid-$50s and have declined modestly over the past month. Analysts note PayPal’s strategic initiatives across Branded, PSP and Venmo should improve profitability by 2026, yet intense competition, some insider selling and mixed financial-stress signals temper the outlook. Investors will watch an upcoming earnings report (expected Feb. 3, 2026) with consensus estimates of about $1.28 EPS and roughly $8.77 billion in revenue for cues on near-term direction.

stories.name: Survey Finds 39% of U.S. Merchants Accept Crypto
stories.summary: A PayPal and National Cryptocurrency Association survey of 619 payment decision-makers found 39% of U.S. merchants accept cryptocurrency at checkout and 84% expect crypto payments to become commonplace within five years. Customer demand is the primary driver: 88% of merchants reported inquiries about paying with crypto and 69% receive such requests at least monthly, with Millennials (77%) and Gen Z (73%) showing the strongest interest; top-adopting sectors include hospitality, travel, digital goods/gaming and retail. Merchants that already accept crypto say it represents about 26% of their sales and roughly 72–75% have seen crypto transaction volumes rise over the past year. Adoption is strongest among large enterprises (about 50% of firms with >$500 million revenue) versus roughly one-third of small and mid-size businesses. PayPal executives said seamless, card-like integration increases merchant value, while complexity remains the main barrier—about 90% said they would adopt crypto if setup and user experience matched traditional credit-card payments.
keyPoints: PayPal launched a crypto checkout tool in July that lets U.S. merchants accept payments in more than 100 cryptocurrencies.
Merchants cited concrete benefits from accepting crypto, including faster transaction speeds (45%), access to new customers (45%), enhanced security (41%), and buyer privacy (40%).

National Cryptocurrency Association President Stu Alderoty said the main obstacle is understanding — not interest — and highlighted partnerships with platforms like PayPal to close knowledge gaps and show crypto can be as simple as conventional payments.

stories.name: Tourism Framed as Economic Infrastructure at FITUR
stories.summary: FITUR 2026 in Madrid reinforced the travel sector's recovery, drawing expanded participation and providing a larger diplomatic and commercial platform for governments and exhibitors to rebuild markets toward pre-pandemic activity. At the World Economic Forum in Davos and at TOURISE, Saudi officials and global industry leaders argued tourism should be treated as economic infrastructure, emphasizing governance, data, long-term investment, and cross-sector partnerships. Saudi Vision 2030 was presented as a working model: the Kingdom reported roughly 30 million inbound visitors in 2025 and pointed to master-planned projects such as AlUla, Diriyah and the Red Sea to scale visitation, protect assets and attract investment. TOURISE convened technology and payments firms at Davos to explore sustainability, digital innovation and safe AI integration across the travel system, and organizers projected tourism's potential as a multi‑trillion‑dollar economic driver. Complementing these global initiatives, the UN World Tourism Barometer signaled rapid destination growth in several markets, and VisitBritain is running targeted trade missions and marketing to disperse visitors to regional, coastal and heritage sites and embed sustainability to boost local economic benefits.
keyPoints: Saudi Arabia has set an ambitious national target of 150 million visitors by 2030; in 2025 the sector already contributed nearly 5% of direct GDP and employed more than one million people, illustrating the scale of tourism’s economic role in the Kingdom.

TOURISE’s Davos programme brought together major technology and payments firms — including Trip.com, Visa, TikTok, PayPal and Salesforce — and hosted sessions such as “Can Tourism Save the World?” and “Agentic Tourism: From Insight to Action” to develop frameworks for safe, connected AI in travel.

Analysts and industry leaders at Davos cited precise macro projections: tourism could grow to a $16 trillion contribution to the global economy by 2034, and currently accounts for about one in every ten dollars of global GDP.

stories.name: PayPal returns to Nigeria via Paga
stories.summary: PayPal has gone live in Nigeria through a partnership with local fintech Paga, allowing users to link PayPal accounts to Paga wallets to receive international payments and withdraw funds locally in naira. The integration ends more than a decade of “send-only” restrictions and legitimizes payments for freelancers, small businesses, and merchants who previously relied on workarounds. Through Paga, users can withdraw PayPal balances, spend via Paga cards, transfer to local banks, pay bills, and merchants can tap PayPal’s global network of over 400 million users to expand internationally. Paga founder and CEO Tayo Oviosu said he first proposed the partnership in 2013, framing the launch as the product of long-term investment in local infrastructure and trust-building. PayPal positions the move as interoperability with local platforms rather than imposing a Western banking model, and it arrives amid broader PayPal investment in Middle East and Africa innovation.
keyPoints: PayPal recently committed $100 million to invest in Middle East and Africa (MEA) innovation, part of broader investment activity in the region.

PayPal’s long ‘send-only’ restriction on Nigerian accounts stemmed from increased fraudulent activity in the early 2000s, which led the company to limit receiving capabilities for users in the country.
Nigeria’s market includes more than 30 million active mobile wallet users, a large user base that PayPal can now access via the Paga integration.

stories.name: Overseas-licensed instant-payout casinos serve UK
stories.summary: Many UK-facing casinos now advertise genuinely fast withdrawals—e-wallets like PayPal, Skrill and Neteller can produce payouts within an hour—though operators warn that KYC verification can delay access until documents are uploaded. Bet Storm is cited as an example that combines rapid payouts with a deposit-match welcome offer (100% up to £200 plus 50 free spins) but requires 10x wagering and prompt KYC to avoid limits. Low-minimum deposit sites (commonly £1–£5) let players stretch small bankrolls and access mobile apps and quick, commission-free cashouts, but those tiny deposit bonuses typically carry heavy wagering requirements. £1 bonuses frequently impose very high playthroughs (reported 50x–200x), so smaller deposits often mean smaller incentives and more restricted bonus value. Players are advised to clear KYC quickly, choose bonuses with lower wagering and favour lower-risk games to protect bankrolls and maximize the benefit of fast-payout, low-deposit offerings.
keyPoints: Bet Storm’s offering includes a very large games library (2,500+ slots), dozens of live dealer tables and a dedicated bingo section, and it supports payment options such as PayviaPhone and PaysafeCard in addition to e‑wallets; KYC documents are uploaded via the Cashier tab in JPEG, PNG or PDF format, and its free spins must be cleared within seven days.
The 10x wagering requirement on Bet Storm’s welcome bonus is notably lower than many UK‑facing sites licensed overseas, which the article says typically carry playthroughs of roughly 35x–50x.

Not all low‑minimum (£1–£5) casinos meet quality standards — reputable low‑deposit sites should guarantee game fairness via certified RNG/software and be evaluated for betting return and overall standards before listing.

Readers are warned to avoid offshore or unlicensed sites that lack consumer protections; U.S. legality varies by state, with places such as Pennsylvania noted for expanding regulated markets. stories.name: Apple Cash Plans Instant-Transfer Fee Hike
stories.summary: Apple has begun notifying Apple Cash users that, beginning February 18, 2026, Instant Transfers will cost 1.7% of the transaction (up from 1.5%) with a $0.25 minimum and a $25 maximum—raising the cap from $15. That change means a $1,000 Instant Transfer will rise from a $15 fee to $17, while standard ACH transfers to a linked bank account will remain free but take one to three business days. The percentage increase is modest, but the higher maximum will make large instant withdrawals noticeably more expensive. Apple says the fee applies only to Instant Transfers from the Wallet app to eligible debit cards and confirms it may adjust pricing again in the future. The move places Apple Cash’s instant-payout costs in line with competitors such as Venmo, PayPal, and Cash App, and users who don’t need immediate access can avoid the fee by using the slower option.
keyPoints: Apple updated the Apple Cash Terms and Conditions on January 23 to reflect the fee change.
The Terms state fees are rounded to the nearest cent and note that no other Apple Cash fees are changing.
Instant Transfers route funds to an eligible debit card via the card's payment network and typically complete within minutes.

stories.name: TSA to Charge $45 ConfirmID Fee Feb. 1
stories.summary: Starting Feb. 1, the Transportation Security Administration will charge a $45 fee for TSA ConfirmID to travelers who do not present a REAL ID or another TSA‑approved form of identification, providing an alternative identity‑verification option at airport checkpoints. ConfirmID typically takes about 10–30 minutes depending on questions and location, can be paid online before arrival, and in some jurisdictions (e.g., Mississippi) is valid for 10 days to cover round‑trip travel. Acceptable IDs that avoid the fee include REAL ID‑compliant driver’s licenses or state photo IDs, U.S. passports, military IDs and DHS trusted traveler cards, and children under 18 generally do not need ID for domestic flights. TSA says the program strengthens transportation security and notes that more than 94% of travelers nationally already present acceptable identification, though state compliance rates vary. Some states are urging passengers to obtain REAL ID; for example, Maryland requires an MVA appointment and in‑person presentation of original or certified documents (scanned uploads are not accepted). Travelers are encouraged to check their state DMV’s REAL ID status and pay online ahead of time to avoid checkpoint delays.
keyPoints: Maryland applicants cannot scan and upload REAL ID documents to the MVA website; they must bring original or certified documents in person by appointment, and the MVA warns that any website claiming to provide upload services is not affiliated with the agency.
TSA and state officials say temporary driver’s licenses are not an acceptable form of identification for boarding domestic flights.

Acting TSA deputy administrator Adam Stahl said TSA Confirm.ID helps keep “terrorists, criminals, and illegal aliens out of the skies and other domestic transportation systems,” framing the program as essential to preventing those threats.

stories.name: PayPal agrees to buy Israeli AI fintech Cymbio
stories.summary: PayPal has agreed to acquire Tel Aviv-based Cymbio to deepen its agentic-commerce capabilities by bringing Cymbio’s technology and team into PayPal’s Store Sync product so merchants’ catalogs and fulfillment logic become discoverable and actionable by AI agents. Cymbio, founded in 2015 with about 80 employees, specializes in dropship automation connecting brands and retailers and is estimated by market sources to be valued in the $150–200 million range. Store Sync integrations already power merchant visibility on Microsoft Copilot and Perplexity, with brands such as Abercrombie & Fitch, Fabletics, Ashley Furniture, Newegg and Adorama live today and support for ChatGPT and Google Gemini expected soon. PayPal, an existing investor in Cymbio, expects the deal to accelerate merchant reach into AI shopping channels and drive product discovery and sales growth. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the acquisition a step forward for agentic commerce but said it will likely make only a small near-term contribution and does not address PayPal’s longer-term loss of consumer checkout share, leaving the firm with an Underweight rating and $51 price target.
keyPoints: PayPal’s acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2026, and the companies have not disclosed the deal terms.

Cymbio was founded by Roy Avidor, Gilad Zirkel and Mor Lavi and has raised under $30 million in its 11 years, with investors including XT Venture Capital (Udi Angel), Vertex, Corner Ventures and PayPal’s venture arm.
Cymbio specializes in dropship automation that connects brands and retailers (helping manage sales and orders) and works with brands such as New Balance, Billabong and Lacoste.

stories.name: Eightfold Sued Over Secret 'Match' AI Scores
stories.summary: Two job seekers, Erin Kistler and Sruti Bhaumik, have filed a proposed nationwide class-action in Contra Costa County alleging Eightfold AI secretly compiles applicants' “Match Scores” (rated 0–5) from LinkedIn, job boards and other online data without disclosing the practice or allowing disputes. The complaint argues those undisclosed rankings are “consumer reports” that violate the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act and California's Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act, and it seeks statutory and actual damages—including $100–$1,000 per federal violation and up to $10,000 per state violation—plus injunctive relief. Plaintiffs and counsel (including Outten & Golden and Towards Justice) say Eightfold draws on massive datasets—reportedly more than a billion profiles and a million job titles and skills—to create talent profiles and scores that can screen candidates out before any human review. The suit cites use of Eightfold by large employers including Microsoft, PayPal, Salesforce, Bayer, Starbucks and Morgan Stanley. Plaintiffs describe concrete harms—qualified applicants who received few or no interview callbacks or automatic rejections—and seek notice, access to underlying data, and the right to correct errors. Legal experts say the case is among the first to test applying consumer-reporting laws to algorithmic hiring tools and could prompt greater transparency and dispute rights for applicants.
keyPoints: The complaint alleges Eightfold pulls a wide range of sensitive personal data beyond resumes — including social media posts, location data, internet activity, tracking cookies and content from sites like GitHub — to evaluate candidates.

David Seligman of Towards Justice described the case as addressing ‘a dystopian AI-driven marketplace, where robots operating behind the scenes are making decisions about the most important things in our lives,’ framing the suit as a civil-rights style challenge to opaque automated decision-making.

According to plaintiffs’ records cited in reporting, Erin Kistler said only about 0.3% of the thousands of applications she submitted resulted in follow-up contact or interviews — a statistic she points to as evidence of concrete, measurable harm.

stories.name: Arknights: Endfield halts PayPal after reported unauthorized charges
stories.summary: Players of the new gacha action game Arknights: Endfield reported unauthorized PayPal charges—ranging from small sums to four-figure losses—shortly after launch, with community posts showing charges in multiple currencies and some users saying other players’ purchases were incorrectly tied to their accounts. Developer Hypergryph and publisher Gryphline acknowledged the problem, apologized, disabled PayPal as a payment option, and said the issue stemmed from inconsistencies between orders and item delivery affecting a small subset of PayPal transactions. On January 22 they traced the first reports, took PayPal offline within hours, reviewed affected transactions and began issuing full refunds for the impacted window, and warned PayPal will remain disabled until the issue is resolved and tested. Impacted players who have not received refunds were instructed to contact customer support (endfield_cs@gryphline.com) with their region and UID for assistance, and the studio said it expects to handle restitution promptly. Several reports noted affected players facing PayPal account flags or identity-verification steps after suspicious activity, and the studio advised using other payment channels while PayPal is offline.
keyPoints: Hypergryph published a detailed timeline of events on January 22, 2026, noting the first player report at 9:58 AM (UTC+8), PayPal was disabled at 11:05 AM (UTC+8), a full review of PayPal transactions was completed at 6:20 PM (UTC+8), and refunds began at 6:30 PM (UTC+8); they also specified refunds cover orders created between 9:36:51 AM and 11:05:36 AM (UTC+8).

The developers said the problem only affected PayPal purchases made through Arknights: Endfield’s official launcher and its official top-up site — PayPal transactions via those channels were the ones reviewed and refunded.

Community screenshots showed transactions billed to a merchant name like “Gryph Fontier PTE. LTD.” and a user-shared list of multi-currency charges (e.g., $9.53 USD, ¥10,000, €33.99, $7.97 CAD, €4.99, etc.), illustrating how varied and international the unauthorized charges appeared.

stories.name: Parklife unveils 2026 headliners Calvin Harris, Skepta
stories.summary: Organisers revealed the complete Parklife 2026 line-up on January 22, confirming Pepsi MAX presents Parklife at Heaton Park across June 20–21 with headliners Calvin Harris, Skepta and breakout Sammy Virji, and a Parklife debut from Zara Larsson. Harris returns for his first Manchester headline in 13 years while promoters emphasise a bill that mixes mainstream crossover names with underground dance, drum-and-bass, house and garage artists. The festival features over 100 acts across multiple stages — including a revamped PANORAMA Stage designed for immersive electronic production — with returning favourites like Rudimental, Josh Baker and Nia Archives alongside heavyweight DJs such as Andy C and Armand Van Helden. Tickets were sold via staged presales (including an exclusive PayPal presale) followed by general sale windows in late January, with weekend tickets starting around £138.50 and day and VIP options available. Organisers and commentators framed the Harris booking as a unifying, high‑tempo centerpiece that underscores Parklife’s status as one of the UK’s largest metropolitan festivals and a summer highlight for national crowds.
keyPoints: Calvin Harris is not only headlining Parklife 2026 but is also scheduled to headline Creamfields over the August Bank Holiday, marking a busy summer festival run.
The new PANORAMA Stage is billed as a multi-level, immersive electronic production featuring curved LED visuals and unique crowd perspectives — and Chris Stussy is set to close that stage.
Josh Baker’s billing reflects a career trajectory at Parklife: after opening the G Stage in 2022 he has been promoted to a Main Stage slot in 2026.

stories.name: PayPal shares slide after Trump plans 10% cap
stories.summary: PayPal’s stock is exposed to concentrated ownership and institutional trading pressure — institutions hold roughly 78% of the company and the top 25 shareholders own about 46% while insiders have been selling, which can amplify price moves. Several analysts have cooled on the name, with Piper Sandler cutting its target to $74 and Daiwa lowering its rating to hold, leaving a MarketBeat consensus of “Hold” and an average target near $76.81. Those downgrades come despite PayPal beating recent quarterly revenue and EPS estimates and maintaining mid-range FY2025 guidance, underscoring mixed fundamental signals. Political risk from President Trump’s proposed one-year 10% cap on credit card rates has pressured financial stocks and contributed to recent share weakness. At the same time, brokers like Mizuho and analysts such as eMarketer see PayPal well-positioned to benefit if consumers shift toward buy-now-pay-later services, which could offset some regulatory and valuation headwinds.
keyPoints: In the most recent quarter PayPal reported EPS of $1.34 (beating the $1.20 consensus by $0.14) and revenue of $8.42 billion (vs. $8.21 billion expected); the firm reported a net margin of 14.96%, return on equity of 25.64% and revenue was up 7.3% year-over-year.

Analyst views are divergent: Royal Bank of Canada raised its target to $91 and rated PayPal 'outperform' while other firms have sharply lowered targets — for example, Citigroup cut its target to $60 and set a 'neutral' rating — highlighting wide disagreement among brokers about PayPal’s outlook.
eMarketer projects PayPal’s buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) volume could exceed $40 billion in 2025, underscoring why some brokers see BNPL expansion as a significant growth avenue for the company.

last_30_days.name: Former Speaker Pelosi PayPal sale precedes 27% drop
last_30_days.summary: Nancy Pelosi’s household reported selling 5,000 shares of PayPal on Dec. 30, 2025 in a periodic filing that listed the transaction in the $250,001–$500,000 range (about $295,000 based on that day’s price). In the weeks after the sale, PayPal shares plunged—falling into the low $40s—after weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter results, soft guidance and an unexpected CEO change. By avoiding holding through that drop, the Pelosis averted an estimated roughly 32% decline (about a $96,000 loss) on that position. Ethics experts note there is no public evidence the trade involved nonpublic information and the sale was disclosed under STOCK Act timelines, but the timing has nonetheless renewed bipartisan calls to restrict or ban individual stock trading by lawmakers. The episode reinforces why Pelosi’s household trades remain closely watched and fuels broader public skepticism about elected officials trading individual stocks.
keyPoints: The Periodic Transaction Report documenting the Dec. 30, 2025 sale was filed with the House Clerk and made public on Jan. 23, 2026.
PayPal’s weak fourth-quarter 2025 fundamentals included revenue of $8.68 billion (below the $8.80 billion consensus) and adjusted EPS of $1.23 (missing the roughly $1.28–$1.29 consensus).
The company announced an unexpected leadership change, naming Enrique Lores as PayPal’s new CEO amid the results-driven selloff.

last_30_days.name: Oxfordshire Woman Nearly Dies From Fake Ozempic
last_30_days.summary: Michelle Sword, 47, of Carterton, Oxfordshire, nearly died after injecting a counterfeit Ozempic pen she purchased on Facebook that contained fast-acting insulin instead of semaglutide, causing her blood sugar to fall to 0.2 mmol/L and sending her into a diabetic coma before paramedics stabilized her. She had previously used genuine Ozempic in 2020 to lose two stone but, facing shortages in 2023, paid £150 via PayPal for a month’s supply from an online seller that arrived two days later. Sword later noticed warning signs she missed — the pen kept clicking and she was unsure of the dose — and has published red flags (including packaging errors and lack of eligibility checks) to warn others against buying prescription drugs from unregulated sources. The UK medicines regulator has seized more than 6,500 fake Ozempic products in just over two years, underscoring the wider, potentially deadly problem of counterfeit weight-loss injections.
keyPoints: Sword remained in hospital overnight after the incident until medics could stabilise her blood sugar levels.
She attributed much of the weight regain to menopause and said she had been having a glass of wine with every meal, which contributed to rising weight to around 10½ stone.

Paramedics spent a prolonged period trying to save her life — reports say they worked for over an hour at the scene, with one account noting a 12‑minute wait for emergency services before they arrived.

last_30_days.name: PayPal Names Enrique Lores; Shares Drop 16–20%
last_30_days.summary: PayPal said Enrique Lores, the former HP CEO, will become its CEO on March 1, with CFO Jamie Miller serving as interim CEO until then and David W. Dorman named independent board chair after the board concluded execution under former CEO Alex Chriss was insufficient. The company reported fourth-quarter revenue of about $8.68 billion and non‑GAAP EPS of $1.23 (vs. $1.28 expected); total payment volume rose roughly 6% to $475.1 billion, while active accounts were roughly flat and transaction frequency fell about 5%, and Branded Checkout growth slowed sharply. Management withdrew its prior 2027 targets and guided 2026 to a mid‑single‑digit EPS decline to flat, citing softer U.S. retail demand, high living costs and intensifying competition. The surprise leadership change, the quarterly miss and the downgraded outlook sent the stock down roughly 16–20%, costing about $10 billion in market value and coinciding with unusually heavy bearish options activity. Board and interim management said Lores’ operational focus should help restore discipline and customer‑centric innovation, but investors remain cautious given macro headwinds and big‑tech wallet competition.
keyPoints: Enrique Lores has served on PayPal’s board for nearly five years and had been board chair since July 2024 prior to being named CEO.

Lores is credited for leading HP’s shift beyond traditional PCs into services, subscriptions and AI-enabled "future-of-work" solutions, and for playing a pivotal role in the separation of HP and HPE while strengthening operating discipline and simplifying cost structure.
Interim CEO Jamie Miller explicitly told investors the board’s decision reflected execution issues, saying, “So the board’s decision is based on execution … our execution is just too slow.”

last_30_days.name: Reports: Multiple US Firms Face Securities Investigations
last_30_days.summary: Multiple law firms have launched investor investigations alleging potential violations of federal securities laws across several public companies. The Law Offices of Frank R. The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith similarly announced investigations for investors in Apollo Global Management and PayPal and is inviting affected shareholders to contact the firm about pursuing claims. All firms are urging investors who suffered losses to reach out to explore potential recovery under the federal securities laws.
keyPoints: Plug Power made a notable company announcement on October 7, 2025 regarding its Chief Executive Officer, which is referenced in the firm’s investigation notice.
Picard Medical’s market-moving disclosure occurred on October 23, 2025 during after-market trading hours, a timing noted in the Frank R. Cruz investigation notice.

Levi & Korsinsky named the replaced PayPal CEO as Alex Chriss and tied the leadership change to the company’s February 3, 2026 announcement that “the pace of change and execution was not in line with the Board's expectations.”

last_30_days.name: Sweepstakes, Crypto Casinos Fill US Market Gaps

last_30_days.name: PayPal Names Enrique Lores CEO; Shares Plunge
last_30_days.summary: PayPal said its Q4 results missed estimates, reporting revenue of $8.68 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.23, while total payment volume rose to about $475.1 billion and active accounts reached roughly 439 million. Growth in higher‑margin branded checkout slowed to about 1% in the holiday quarter, a concern management and investors highlighted amid competition from Stripe, Apple and others. Citing that the pace of change and execution "was not in line with the Board's expectations," the board named Enrique Lores—former HP CEO and former PayPal board chair—as President and CEO effective March 1, with CFO/COO Jamie Miller serving as interim until then. The results and leadership change prompted a sharp market reaction, with shares plunging roughly mid‑teens to about 18% to lows not seen since early 2017, extending a yearlong decline. PayPal gave modest fiscal‑2026 guidance (reports put EPS around $5.75) and warned of a mid‑single‑digit EPS decline in Q1 and a low‑single‑digit to flat full‑year outcome. The board and new leadership face pressure to accelerate product execution and respond to softer consumer spending and intensifying Big Tech threats to its payments franchise.
keyPoints: This quarter marked PayPal’s first earnings miss in roughly two years, a notable break in the company’s recent streak of meeting or beating estimates.
Management said the underperformance in branded checkout was driven by weakness in U.S. retail, international headwinds and tough year‑ago comparisons in high‑growth verticals.
Total payment volume rose about 9% year‑over‑year (6% on a currency‑neutral basis) to $475.1 billion.

last_30_days.name: Golden Nugget launches Ontario online casino

last_30_days.name: Survey Finds 39% of U.S. Merchants Accept Crypto
last_30_days.summary: A PayPal and National Cryptocurrency Association survey of 619 payment decision-makers found 39% of U.S. merchants accept cryptocurrency at checkout and 84% expect crypto payments to become commonplace within five years. Customer demand is the primary driver: 88% of merchants reported inquiries about paying with crypto and 69% receive such requests at least monthly, with Millennials (77%) and Gen Z (73%) showing the strongest interest; top-adopting sectors include hospitality, travel, digital goods/gaming and retail. Merchants that already accept crypto say it represents about 26% of their sales and roughly 72–75% have seen crypto transaction volumes rise over the past year. PayPal executives said seamless, card-like integration increases merchant value, while complexity remains the main barrier—about 90% said they would adopt crypto if setup and user experience matched traditional credit-card payments.

last_30_days.name: TSA to Charge $45 ConfirmID Fee Feb. 1
last_30_days.summary: Starting Feb. 1, the Transportation Security Administration will charge a $45 fee for TSA ConfirmID to travelers who do not present a REAL ID or another TSA‑approved form of identification, providing an alternative identity‑verification option at airport checkpoints. ConfirmID typically takes about 10–30 minutes depending on questions and location, can be paid online before arrival, and in some jurisdictions (e.g., Mississippi) is valid for 10 days to cover round‑trip travel. Acceptable IDs that avoid the fee include REAL ID‑compliant driver’s licenses or state photo IDs, U.S. passports, military IDs and DHS trusted traveler cards, and children under 18 generally do not need ID for domestic flights. TSA says the program strengthens transportation security and notes that more than 94% of travelers nationally already present acceptable identification, though state compliance rates vary. Some states are urging passengers to obtain REAL ID; for example, Maryland requires an MVA appointment and in‑person presentation of original or certified documents (scanned uploads are not accepted). Travelers are encouraged to check their state DMV’s REAL ID status and pay online ahead of time to avoid checkpoint delays.
keyPoints: Maryland applicants cannot scan and upload REAL ID documents to the MVA website; they must bring original or certified documents in person by appointment, and the MVA warns that any website claiming to provide upload services is not affiliated with the agency.
TSA and state officials say temporary driver’s licenses are not an acceptable form of identification for boarding domestic flights.

Acting TSA deputy administrator Adam Stahl said TSA Confirm.ID helps keep “terrorists, criminals, and illegal aliens out of the skies and other domestic transportation systems,” framing the program as essential to preventing those threats.

last_30_days.name: PayPal agrees to buy Israeli AI fintech Cymbio
last_30_days.summary: PayPal has agreed to acquire Tel Aviv-based Cymbio to deepen its agentic-commerce capabilities by bringing Cymbio’s technology and team into PayPal’s Store Sync product so merchants’ catalogs and fulfillment logic become discoverable and actionable by AI agents. Cymbio, founded in 2015 with about 80 employees, specializes in dropship automation connecting brands and retailers and is estimated by market sources to be valued in the $150–200 million range. Store Sync integrations already power merchant visibility on Microsoft Copilot and Perplexity, with brands such as Abercrombie & Fitch, Fabletics, Ashley Furniture, Newegg and Adorama live today and support for ChatGPT and Google Gemini expected soon. PayPal, an existing investor in Cymbio, expects the deal to accelerate merchant reach into AI shopping channels and drive product discovery and sales growth. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the acquisition a step forward for agentic commerce but said it will likely make only a small near-term contribution and does not address PayPal’s longer-term loss of consumer checkout share, leaving the firm with an Underweight rating and $51 price target.
keyPoints: PayPal’s acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2026, and the companies have not disclosed the deal terms.

Cymbio was founded by Roy Avidor, Gilad Zirkel and Mor Lavi and has raised under $30 million in its 11 years, with investors including XT Venture Capital (Udi Angel), Vertex, Corner Ventures and PayPal’s venture arm.
Cymbio specializes in dropship automation that connects brands and retailers (helping manage sales and orders) and works with brands such as New Balance, Billabong and Lacoste.

last_30_days.name: Eightfold Sued Over Secret 'Match' AI Scores
last_30_days.summary: Two job seekers, Erin Kistler and Sruti Bhaumik, have filed a proposed nationwide class-action in Contra Costa County alleging Eightfold AI secretly compiles applicants' “Match Scores” (rated 0–5) from LinkedIn, job boards and other online data without disclosing the practice or allowing disputes. The complaint argues those undisclosed rankings are “consumer reports” that violate the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act and California's Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act, and it seeks statutory and actual damages—including $100–$1,000 per federal violation and up to $10,000 per state violation—plus injunctive relief. Plaintiffs and counsel (including Outten & Golden and Towards Justice) say Eightfold draws on massive datasets—reportedly more than a billion profiles and a million job titles and skills—to create talent profiles and scores that can screen candidates out before any human review. The suit cites use of Eightfold by large employers including Microsoft, PayPal, Salesforce, Bayer, Starbucks and Morgan Stanley. Plaintiffs describe concrete harms—qualified applicants who received few or no interview callbacks or automatic rejections—and seek notice, access to underlying data, and the right to correct errors. Legal experts say the case is among the first to test applying consumer-reporting laws to algorithmic hiring tools and could prompt greater transparency and dispute rights for applicants.
keyPoints: The complaint alleges Eightfold pulls a wide range of sensitive personal data beyond resumes — including social media posts, location data, internet activity, tracking cookies and content from sites like GitHub — to evaluate candidates.

David Seligman of Towards Justice described the case as addressing ‘a dystopian AI-driven marketplace, where robots operating behind the scenes are making decisions about the most important things in our lives,’ framing the suit as a civil-rights style challenge to opaque automated decision-making.

According to plaintiffs’ records cited in reporting, Erin Kistler said only about 0.3% of the thousands of applications she submitted resulted in follow-up contact or interviews — a statistic she points to as evidence of concrete, measurable harm.

last_30_days.name: Arknights: Endfield halts PayPal after reported unauthorized charges

Developer Hypergryph and publisher Gryphline acknowledged the problem, apologized, disabled PayPal as a payment option, and said the issue stemmed from inconsistencies between orders and item delivery affecting a small subset of PayPal transactions. On January 22 they traced the first reports, took PayPal offline within hours, reviewed affected transactions and began issuing full refunds for the impacted window, and warned PayPal will remain disabled until the issue is resolved and tested. Impacted players who have not received refunds were instructed to contact customer support (endfield_cs@gryphline.com) with their region and UID for assistance, and the studio said it expects to handle restitution promptly. Several reports noted affected players facing PayPal account flags or identity-verification steps after suspicious activity, and the studio advised using other payment channels while PayPal is offline.
keyPoints: Hypergryph published a detailed timeline of events on January 22, 2026, noting the first player report at 9:58 AM (UTC+8), PayPal was disabled at 11:05 AM (UTC+8), a full review of PayPal transactions was completed at 6:20 PM (UTC+8), and refunds began at 6:30 PM (UTC+8); they also specified refunds cover orders created between 9:36:51 AM and 11:05:36 AM (UTC+8).

The developers said the problem only affected PayPal purchases made through Arknights: Endfield’s official launcher and its official top-up site — PayPal transactions via those channels were the ones reviewed and refunded.

Community screenshots showed transactions billed to a merchant name like “Gryph Fontier PTE. LTD.” and a user-shared list of multi-currency charges (e.g., $9.53 USD, ¥10,000, €33.99, $7.97 CAD, €4.99, etc.), illustrating how varied and international the unauthorized charges appeared.

last_30_days.name: PayPal shares slide after Trump plans 10% cap
last_30_days.summary: PayPal’s stock is exposed to concentrated ownership and institutional trading pressure — institutions hold roughly 78% of the company and the top 25 shareholders own about 46% while insiders have been selling, which can amplify price moves. Several analysts have cooled on the name, with Piper Sandler cutting its target to $74 and Daiwa lowering its rating to hold, leaving a MarketBeat consensus of “Hold” and an average target near $76.81. Those downgrades come despite PayPal beating recent quarterly revenue and EPS estimates and maintaining mid-range FY2025 guidance, underscoring mixed fundamental signals. Political risk from President Trump’s proposed one-year 10% cap on credit card rates has pressured financial stocks and contributed to recent share weakness. At the same time, brokers like Mizuho and analysts such as eMarketer see PayPal well-positioned to benefit if consumers shift toward buy-now-pay-later services, which could offset some regulatory and valuation headwinds.
keyPoints: In the most recent quarter PayPal reported EPS of $1.34 (beating the $1.20 consensus by $0.14) and revenue of $8.42 billion (vs. $8.21 billion expected); the firm reported a net margin of 14.96%, return on equity of 25.64% and revenue was up 7.3% year-over-year.

Analyst views are divergent: Royal Bank of Canada raised its target to $91 and rated PayPal 'outperform' while other firms have sharply lowered targets — for example, Citigroup cut its target to $60 and set a 'neutral' rating — highlighting wide disagreement among brokers about PayPal’s outlook.
eMarketer projects PayPal’s buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) volume could exceed $40 billion in 2025, underscoring why some brokers see BNPL expansion as a significant growth avenue for the company.
